P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: Generally free. Both Liberian and US dollars are legal tender under a managed float, and there are no restrictions on converting or transferring investment-related funds (trade.gov). Rules for individuals' service income were not captured.

sources.title: Liberia Country Commercial Guide — Trade Financing
sources.quote: Liberia has a managed floating exchange rate system, with Liberian and U.S. dollars being legal tender.

P2_fcy_account.question: Can resident individuals hold a foreign-currency account locally?
P2_fcy_account.answer: Not established in a captured source (USD accounts are common in practice).

P3_local_gateways.question: Which local payment gateways can an individual or sole trader use to accept online payments?
P3_local_gateways.answer: Global platform availability for Liberia (automated collector snapshots, Oct 2026). Available: Paddle (not on its exclusion list; software sellers only, each seller reviewed); Dodo Payments (sellers); Google Play (developer registration). Not listed: Stripe (merchant sign-up); Lemon Squeezy payouts; Polar (payouts); Whop (payouts); Etsy seller payments; YouTube Partner Program.

L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: Businesses register at the Liberia Business Registry (LBR) in Monrovia and obtain a TIN. Registrations are valid for 12 months and must be renewed annually; trading without valid registration risks fines. A government fee schedule reportedly lists US$700 for a sole proprietorship, conflicting with other figures (not confirmed).

L2_tax_id.answer: A TIN is obtained when registering the business (LRA); a business should hold only one TIN.

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: A resident's gross income includes all income from whatever source derived (worldwide). Resident rates: nil up to LRD 70,000, then 5%, 15% and 25% above LRD 800,000. A presumptive regime for small taxpayers was not captured.

sources.title: Liberia - Individual - Taxes on personal income
sources.quote: Gross income of a resident natural person includes all income from whatever source derived, such as wages, business profits, rents, dividends, and interest, unless specifically excluded by the Revenue Code.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: GST on services is 13% (raised from 12%), with telecoms at 15% (LRA notice, 2026). Liberia is replacing GST with a full VAT: registration opened 1 July 2026 and VAT takes effect 1 January 2027. Registration threshold and VAT rate were not confirmed.

sources.title: Important Revenue Notice: Adjustment to Goods and Services Tax (GST) Rates
sources.quote: The updated framework introduces a 13 percent GST on services while maintaining the rate on telecommunications services at 15 percent.

sources.title: Important Revenue Notice: Adjustment to GST Rates
sources.quote: The new GST rate represents a modest adjustment from the previous 12 percent rate, reflecting a gradual and balanced approach to strengthening domestic revenue while maintaining affordability for consumers and businesses.

sources.title: Transition de la GST à la TVA au Libéria (22 Jul 2026)
sources.quote: Le Libéria remplace sa Taxe sur les biens et services (GST) par un régime complet de Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée (TVA), avec une ouverture des enregistrements le 1er juillet 2026 et la mise en œuvre du nouveau système le 1er janvier 2027.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; PayPal is not available; Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (4) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
